sections.content:
152,865 people

were counted on the census as "hairdressers and barbers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Hairdressers and barbers shampoo, cut, colour, style and treat hair.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "hairdressers and barbers" there were more women than men (80.4% compared with 19.6%).

This means "hairdressers and barbers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "leisure, travel and related personal service occupations".

Men made up 19.6% and women made up 80.4% of "hairdressers and barbers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "hairdressers and barbers" included:

  • animal care services occupations (other)
  • office managers
  • houseparents and residential wardens

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "hairdressers and barbers", 15.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "hairdressers and barbers" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "hairdressers and barbers" included:

  • warehouse operatives
  • air-conditioning and refrigeration installers and repairers
  • security system installers and repairers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "hairdressers and barbers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "hairdressers and barbers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "hairdressers and barbers", 8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (60.3% compared with 39.7%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (59.1%) than an employee (40.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
